mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for 4 consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to expected equity cash flows, lowering the present value of future dividends and earnings, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 4.5% for 6 consecutive months signals accommodative monetary policy, lowering the cost of capital and increasing the present value of expected equity cash flows, which produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 50,000 jobs for 3 consecutive months indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
